label: Digitally Immersed & Emotionally Distressed
summary: This profile represents highly educated women who spend more than 5 hours daily online and report elevated levels of loneliness, depressive symptoms, and anxiety. Their UCLA-8 loneliness score (1.74), PHQ-9 depression score (1.75), and GAD-7 anxiety score (2.17) all sit in the higher range, suggesting a pattern of co-occurring emotional distress. With 165 respondents in this cluster, it represents a substantial subgroup where heavy digital engagement coincides with pronounced psychological vulnerability across all three measured dimensions.
demographic_anchor: Female, graduate-level education or above, daily screen/internet use exceeding 5 hours
behavior_markers: Heavy daily digital engagement (more than 5 hours)
Elevated loneliness despite high connectivity (UCLA-8 mean 1.74)
Notably high anxiety symptoms, the most pronounced distress indicator (GAD-7 mean 2.17)
Co-occurrence of loneliness, depression, and anxiety suggesting compounded emotional burden
Highly educated yet reporting significant psychological distress
tone: Anxious, isolated, and emotionally burdened despite high educational attainment and extensive online presence

label: Well-Adjusted Male Graduate
summary: This profile represents respondents who report consistently low levels of loneliness, depressive symptoms, and anxiety symptoms. They score well below typical thresholds on all three psychological distress measures, suggesting a generally positive mental health status with minimal emotional distress.
demographic_anchor: Male, graduate-level education or above, 1–3 hours of daily screen/internet use
behavior_markers: Very low loneliness scores (UCLA-8 mean ≈ 0.77 on normalized scale)
Moderate and controlled daily screen or internet usage (1–3 hours)
Higher educational attainment associated with stable psychological functioning

label: Lonely but Emotionally Resilient
summary: This profile captures respondents who report notably elevated loneliness yet maintain relatively low levels of depressive and anxiety symptoms. Despite feeling socially disconnected, they do not exhibit the affective distress typically associated with loneliness, suggesting a degree of emotional resilience or effective coping that buffers against mood and anxiety disorders.
demographic_anchor: Predominantly female, holding graduate-level education or above, with moderate daily screen/internet use of 1–3 hours
behavior_markers: Elevated loneliness scores (UCLA-8 mean ≈ 1.30) indicating frequent feelings of social disconnection
Low depressive symptom severity (PHQ-9 mean ≈ 0.86) suggesting minimal mood disturbance
Low anxiety symptom severity (GAD-7 mean ≈ 0.91) indicating limited worry or nervousness
Moderate internet/screen engagement (1–3 hours daily), not excessive
Apparent decoupling between social isolation feelings and clinical-level psychological distress
tone: Quietly detached yet psychologically stable; socially understimulated rather than emotionally overwhelmed
